Most people believe cannibalism is one of the most barbaric things to ever walk this earth. I see cannibalism as a logical thing to do. Not in the sense of killing people for their meat, but rather using the meat of healthy people who have passed from accidents. The meat can be salvaged from those in fatal accidents. The meat, though some may be bad (broken bones, internal hemorrhaging, etc), the rest can still be salvaged. The meat could be used to help feed people that are starving or just want a taste. Though most people would never eat it, there are people that would as it isn't too discernible from pork. Human meat even has a name for it "long pork".

You would also have the benefit of saving money on a funeral or cremation. A company could offer an incentive for offering your body for food, such as paying your beneficiary a lump some for the body. Maybe a loan that would be given to you between a certain age, if you passed in this time for non medical reasons you would have no obligation to pay them back, but if you live past that age you are required to pay them back.

Burying and cremating a human body is a waste. Why not use it for good once someone passes? It's just recycling.

Cannibalism could be productive, except for the fact that it would spread a terrible amount of diseases. Most livestock pathogens are completely harmless to people which makes eating them safely much easier.

The only disease that I can find that would cause problems is Kuru which is from eating nerve tissue. Most highly concentrated in the brain and spine. Both could easily be avoided. Though there is still a potential risk for it, it is severely less.

Any other pathogens such as viruses, bacteria, pathogens, would be destroyed with cooking like any other meat.
With so many people being obese and unhealthy it would not be profitable to do such a thing. The traditional meat would be healthier than human meat and it's already unhealthy imo.

I wouldn't eat a dead or chronically ill human as there would be diseases and viruses that I wouldn't know even know about about by just looking at their skin/shell. Who knows how long someone has been lying out there for and how many flies that feed off of feces have touched that body. Their body would have decomposed slightly and maggots are not something you want to be eating.

Even if they haven't been lying out there in the open, would you give your dead grandmother to another family so that they can eat her remains? It sounds morally incorrect to myself and you'd feel very uncomfortable knowing that someone is eating a dead relative of yours as if they were having a regular meal. If you were given a human to eat, deep fried and cooked medium rare, served with a side of lemon, how absurd would that be? It makes me laugh just thinking about it.

Many people find it disturbing, and many think that if they find something disturbing, then it is wrong. If you assume animals have an associated conscious awareness, then salvaging meat from people who died is rationally much better than raising animals for slaughter or even hunting animals. I'm still not sure I'd be willing to eat it though.
